Creates a new Databricks classification job using Google DLP. Scans all accessible catalogs and tables in the connected Databricks workspace.

**GDLP collection:** Optionally specify `collection_name` to restrict classification to the infoTypes defined in that collection. When omitted, all default Google DLP infoTypes are used.

Creates a new agent-based (OLTP) classification job. Requires an agent_id identifying the classification agent, repository connection details, and service user credentials.

Creates a new Snowflake-based classification job.

**Classification type:** Controls which classification engine runs the job.
- `altr_native` (default when omitted): ALTR's built-in regex classification via Snowflake UDFs. Requires `collection_name` and `job_type`.
- `gdlp`: Google DLP-powered classification hosted by ALTR. Does not require `job_type` (defaults to FULL). Optionally accepts `collection_name` to scope which infoTypes are inspected.

info.name: List classification decisions for a job

params.description: Scope filter: limit decisions to this database (top of the contiguous scope chain)

params.description: Scope filter: limit to this schema (requires database)

params.name: table
params.description: Scope filter: limit to this table (requires schema)

params.name: column
params.description: Scope filter: limit to this column (requires table)

params.name: limit
params.description: Maximum number of decisions to return (default: 100, max: 1000)

items.docs: Retrieves a paginated flat list of classification decisions recorded for the job, across all classifiers and all cascade levels. Optionally scope the result to an object subtree with the database/schema/table/column query params — the scope chain must be contiguous (a column filter requires table, schema, and database). A scoped read returns only that subtree's decisions without paginating past the rest. The classifier axis is not filterable. Use next_page_token to fetch subsequent pages.

Records an approve or reject decision for a job. A decision targets an object path (database, schema, table, column — contiguous from the database down) and may additionally narrow to a single classifier via classifier_name, an optional filter at any object level. Examples: {database} approves every classifier under the database; {database, classifier_name} approves one classifier across the whole database; {database, schema, table, column, classifier_name} is the match scope. Removes a previously-recorded decision and decrements the corresponding rollup counters at all populated levels. Returns 404 if the decision does not exist; revocation is explicit failure, not idempotent. Request body carries the same identifier fields as POST. Note: DELETE-with-body is HTTP-legal (RFC 9110 §9.3.5) but unusual for some HTTP clients/proxies; document the contract here.

params.description: Filter by decision status: approved/rejected keep rows decided that status — a decision of that status in the subtree, or an ancestor object decision covering the row; pending keeps rows that are not fully decided

items.docs: Returns the root level of the findings tree — sorted list of databases under this job. Each row carries distinct_classifier_count, findings_count (the (column × classifier) leaf count in the subtree — a column matched by N classifiers counts as N findings; reflects the classifier filter when one is supplied), and aggregated match_rate_avg for its subtree. Optional multi-value filter classifier_name (repeat the query param to OR multiple values).

Creates a new classification job report for a specific job.

Cancels a review-gated job (created with requires_review=true) while it is still in the review lifecycle (PROCESSING_FINDINGS or AWAITING_REVIEW), transitioning the job to CANCELLED and reclaiming its review substrate. Rejects a job whose confirm has already been accepted (PROCESSING_REPORT), a terminal job, or a non-gated job. The report-scoped counterpart to POST /jobs/{job_id}/report/confirm.

Accepts confirmation for a review-gated job (created with requires_review=true). Verifies every finding has a decision, then queues async generation of the consumable report (rejected object × classifier findings excluded) by transitioning the job to PROCESSING_REPORT. Returns 202 immediately; clients poll job status until COMPLETED, at which point report_status is confirmed. Only valid while the report is in_review; once accepted, decisions are locked.

info.name: Get review progress for a job

items.docs: Returns total/approved/rejected/pending counts for the job's review progress. approved/rejected are FINDINGS covered by decisions (resolved through the most-specific-wins decision cascade), not raw decision counts — an object-scope decision covers every finding beneath it. Counts come from the materialized findings-index rollups (no full scan).

info.name: Get classification summary for a job

items.docs: Returns the per-classifier counts and column totals for a job. Equivalent to the data in summary.json but delivered inline as a snake_case JSON body so callers do not need to follow a presigned URL. For an HitL-gated job (`requires_review`) still awaiting confirmation, the summary is derived from the review substrate so it is available before the report is confirmed — its counts are UNFILTERED (they reflect the full scan, not the post-confirm decision-filtered report).
